bull.b: Broad top-line growth, led by e-commerce and subscriptions, indicates improving customer acquisition and product adoption. Expansion across direct channels can strengthen distribution economics and create a larger recurring customer base, supporting revenue durability if momentum persists.

The sharp margin improvement shows better channel mix, pricing discipline, and favorable product economics. A structurally higher gross margin gives SenesTech more potential to absorb operating costs, reinvest in growth, and narrow losses as revenue scales.

Building internal e-commerce, sales, marketing, and assessment capabilities expands the company’s commercial infrastructure beyond product distribution alone. These initiatives may improve customer reach and support repeatable B2B conversion over the next several quarters.

bear.b: Large losses relative to revenue show that the current cost structure has not reached operating scale, despite stronger gross margins. Persistent unprofitability limits internally funded investment and leaves future performance highly dependent on substantial revenue growth or cost reduction.

Ongoing cash consumption reduces financial flexibility and may require external funding before the business reaches profitability. Although burn improved recently, a limited runway increases execution pressure and makes sustained improvement in revenue and expenses important to business continuity.

Failure to meet Nasdaq’s minimum bid requirement creates a continuing listing-compliance risk through the stated cure period. Potential delisting could complicate financing access, increase administrative pressure, and distract management while the company is still funding losses.
